notes: CREDIT = FULL RETAIL, 1:1 kWh with monthly rollover (Xcel, Black Hills). Annual surplus at true-up paid at avoided cost (Xcel) unless customer elects rollover/donation. Co-ops/munis differ.

Idaho Power (largest IOU), residential Schedule 6: real-time net billing since Jan 2024; exports credited at an avoided-cost, time-of-day export credit rate (not a fixed % of retail). Rate cut ~31% effective Oct 1, 2025; next update deferred to 2028. Avista residential: monthly net metering at retail. Rocky Mountain Power residential: nominally net billing but reported (EnergySage, unverified) as still ~full retail for systems <25 kW.

CREDIT = 75% OF RETAIL on net excess (NV Energy Tier 4, AB 405; locked 20 yrs). Netting interval differs: Sierra Pacific (north) uses 15-minute netting for new customers approved on/after Oct 1, 2025; Nevada Power (south) keeps monthly netting but added a 15-min peak demand charge Apr 2026. Sources conflicted on Nevada Power netting.

CREDIT IS PARTIAL, NOT A FLAT %: exports credited at 100% supply + 100% transmission + 25% distribution (NEM 2.0/2.1, NHPUC Order 27074, Nov 2024); same across Eversource, Unitil, Liberty. Effective % of retail varies by utility; ~85% is cited only by installer marketing sites (unverified).
Residential customers remain on monthly net metering. Striping likely reflects non-residential rules (excluded). Residential credit value not verified as full retail.

PGE and Pacific Power residential: monthly kWh net metering at retail. Reason for DSIRE striping unverified; possibly Idaho Power's Oregon territory (filed Feb 2024 to adopt its Idaho net billing; outcome not found).
